az_5_bishop.blurb: Bishop is a small, steep wall on the Chessman side of Mount Lemmon in the Santa Catalina Mountains, with seven routes: six sport lines and a single trad line. Grades run from 5.9 into the 5.12s, with a handful of 5.10 and 5.11 climbs between, so it suits climbers who already lead the harder end of the sport scale. The main face is a vertical red wall and stays in shade until early afternoon. It sits at roughly 5,200 feet, which makes it a comfortable choice when lower crags are hot. The walk in is short but steep and involves a little scrambling.
az_5_bishop.approach: From the roadside pullout, climb straight up the rocky drainage for about 15 minutes, with some scrambling. Where the trail splits near the cliff, take the level right-hand branch; Bishop is the first wall you reach.

az_cat_s_cradle.blurb: Cat's Cradle is a small trad crag tucked behind the Fist Pinnacle hillside in the West Stronghold of Cochise Stronghold, near Council Rocks. It holds seven trad routes, from an easy 5.6 up to 5.11, though most fall around 5.10. The wall is cut by many crack systems, and its sheltered cove, with trees and boulders around it, gives plenty of shade and blocks the wind. It is hidden from the parking lot, so expect a long, route-finding approach of around 45 minutes that passes through chasms and a fourth-class ledge system before you reach the base.

az_cactus_ranch.blurb: Cactus Ranch is a low-elevation crag on the lower Catalina Highway of Mount Lemmon, above Tucson, in Sonoran Desert terrain. It has seven routes, six of them sport and one trad, at moderate grades from 5.7 up to 5.10, each roughly 50 to 75 feet tall with lower-off anchors. The base has a flat spot to hang out under a shady mesquite, and the views across the city are excellent. The wall is in shade in the morning and picks up sun around midday in winter, which is when this crag is at its best.

az_expansion_pack_the.blurb: The Expansion Pack is a newer fin in the Crags Against Humanity zone on the lower Catalina Highway of Mount Lemmon, up and to the left of the Draw Pile. It has seven routes, six sport and one trad, running from 5.10 to 5.12 with most in the 5.11 and 5.12 range. Expect gentle overhangs with big holds that lead to technical moves once the wall steepens, so the pump and the angle are the challenge. The wider crag is shaded from about mid-morning and gets a lot of traffic, though this harder fin is a step up from the easy routes elsewhere.
